newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU free-market barley export bids total 551,300 T.
newsitem.headline: EU free-market barley export bids total 551,300 T.

text.p: Grain traders bid to export a total of 551,300 tonnes of barley from the European Union free market at subsidies ranging from 26.98 to 38.47 Ecus per tonne at this week's grain tenders, EU grain industry sources said on Thursday.
But the offer for the lowest refund was limited to 2,000 tonnes, they said.
EU exporters bid to export around 70,000 tonnes of barley at a refund of below 30 Ecus per tonne.

The highest bids were made in France, where one offer was submitted for 150,000 tonnes of barley at a refund of 34.87 Ecus per tonne and a second was placed for 150,000 tonnes at a refund of 38.47 Ecus.
Industry sources thought it unlikely that the EU would grant large tonnages of barley in view of the high refunds asked.
They suggested the Commission might grant at best 5,000 tonnes of barley with refunds of under 30 Ecus per tonne.
Last Thursday the EU granted 46,000 tonnes of free-market barley at a maximum refund of 24.99 Ecus per tonne, worth $142 fob on world markets.
The French national grain office ONIC earlier reported that traders bid to export 496,000 tonnes of EU barley through France at refunds ranging from 29.77 to 38.47 Ecus per tonne.
German traders also bid for 3,000 tonnes of free market barley at a restitution of 27.14 Ecus, and there were other unspecified bids from elsewhere in the EU.
In addition, German traders bid to export 52,509 tonnes of intervention barley at minimum prices ranging from 100.37 to 108.31 Ecus per tonne, EU grain industry sources said.
The German intervention board BLE had reported bids for 221,000 tonnes of intervention barley but said they included multiple bids for identical lots.
